title: Fred Richard coasts to first national title at US gymnastics championships | Gymnastics | The Guardian
description: Richard held off Shane Wiskus and Danila Leykin to claim his first national crown, two years after helping the US win Olympic bronze in Paris
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Richard held off Shane Wiskus and Danila Leykin to claim his first national crown, two years after helping the US win Olympic bronze in Paris
Content: Fred Richard smiles after competing in the men's rings during the US gymnastics championships on Saturday night.Photograph: Ross D Franklin/APView image in fullscreenFred Richard smiles after competing in the men's rings during the US gymnastics championships on Saturday night.Photograph: Ross D Franklin/APGymnasticsFred Richard coasts to first national title at US gymnastics championships22-year-old finishes two points clear of Shane WiskusParis bronze medalist rebounds from difficult 2025Nedoroscik falters as Hoopes wins pommel horse goldAgenciesSun 9 Aug 2026 00.10 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleFrederick Richard won his first US men’s gymnastics all-around title Saturday night, flashing the form he believes can make him a contender at the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.The 22-year-old Richard, a key member of the men’s team that earned bronze at the Paris Games two summers ago, posted a two-day total of 170.015, two points clear of runner-up Shane Wiskus and three points ahead of promising newcomer Danila Leykin.Skye Blakely and Claire Pease share lead at US gymnastics championshipsRead moreThe charismatic, socially-media savvy Richard has made it his mission to bring his sport to a larger audience. That includes breaking norms – and the rules – by ditching the traditional stirrup pants on a handful of events in favor of shorts and compression leggings, all under a singlet featuring his “Frederick Flips” logo.The fashion statement costs Richard three-tenths (0.3) every competition he does it, a move that he has unequivocally said is worth it to bring visibility to a side of the sport that often operates in the shadow of the more popular women’s program.After Thursday night’s opening round – when he found himself just two-tenths (0.2) ahead of the 19-year-old Leykin – Richard doubled down, saying he would sacrifice a national championship if that’s what it came to.“I’m not here to say everybody should wear this uniform,” Richard said after night one. “I’m just here to say it’s not hurting gymnastics.”Fortunately for Richard, he didn’t have to choose. His confident performance across six rotations on Saturday marked the latest step forward in a comeback year after a disappointing 2025 in which he found himself left off both the national and world championship teams.View image in fullscreenFred Richard competes in the men’s pommel horse during the US gymnastics championships on Saturday night.Photograph: Ross D Franklin/APThe experience was sobering for a gymnast who wants to be the face of a men’s program looking to make some noise in Los Angeles in a couple of years. He responded by putting in the work, and it paid off during two days in the desert in which he held off challenges from the promising Leykin and Wiskus, a 2020 Olympian who returned to competition this year following a break after being an Olympic alternate in 2024.‘It just means more’: Black college gymnasts competing in a divided southRead moreLeykin began the finals with a flourish, scoring a 14.963 following a stylish high bar set that briefly put the pressure on Richard. Yet his bid to finish atop the all-around podium ended on floor, where he shuffled at the end of his first tumbling pass and sat down after his second, his 11.650 giving Richard plenty of breathing room.Not that Richard needed it. His thrilling high bar set that included three technically intricate releases ended with a 15.005 score, the second best of the night on the apparatus behind Cooper Kim. He had no issues tumbling on a floor that gave others in the fields fits, and when he survived pommel horse without any mishaps – hardly a given – he celebrated by pumping up the crowd. His total of 14.633 allowed him to use the final two rotations as a victory lap of sorts.When he cleanly hit his vault in the final rotation, he turned toward the crowd and flashed the “No 1” sign after saluting the judges, the first of what he hopes are multiple national titles during a career still on the ascent finally secure.Richard is basically assured of a spot on the team that will head to the Netherlands in October for the world championships. Leykin is likely close to a lock.Stephen Nedoroscik, the pommel horse specialist whose performance in Paris helped the Americans clinch their first team medal at the Olympics in 16 years and shot him to fame in the process, will likely be watching from home.Competing with the goggles that have long been his trademark and still recovering from multiple injuries that have slowed his training, Nedoroscik came off the horse midway through his routine on Saturday and his two-day total of 28.366 put him well behind gold medalist Patrick Hoopes, who has – for now at least – supplanted Nedoroscik as the best American on a demanding apparatus that is often pivotal in international competitions.Explore more on these topicsGymnasticsUS sportsShareReuse this content

title: ‘I’m not ready to compete’: Jannik Sinner pulls out of Cincinnati Open | Jannik Sinner | The Guardian
description: The men’s world No 1 has withdrawn from tournament with a knee injury, and is trying to stay fit for the US Open which starts on 30 August
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: The men’s world No 1 has withdrawn from tournament with a knee injury, and is trying to stay fit for the US Open which starts on 30 August
Content: Jannik Sinner has not played since beating Alexander Zverev in July to retain his Wimbledon title.Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The GuardianView image in fullscreenJannik Sinner has not played since beating Alexander Zverev in July to retain his Wimbledon title.Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The GuardianJannik Sinner‘I’m not ready to compete’: Jannik Sinner pulls out of Cincinnati OpenWorld No 1 out of tournament with knee injuryItalian trying to stay fit for US Open which starts 30 AugustAFPSun 9 Aug 2026 13.04 EDTLast modified on Sun 9 Aug 2026 14.27 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThe World No 1,Jannik Sinner, has pulled out of the Cincinnati Open due to a right knee injury, the Italian announced on Sunday.“After consulting with my doctors and my team, I have to announce that I need to withdraw from the Masters 1000 tournament in Cincinnati,” he said in a statement posted on the ATP website. “My right knee has been bothering me and even though we have been working hard with my medical team, I have to accept that I’m not ready to compete yet.”Game, set, Chat: how tennis players use AI to scout opponents and run their livesRead moreThe tournament begins on Thursday, the same day as the end of the Masters event in Montreal, which Sinner also missed. The five-time Grand Slam winner had been on a six-tournament winning streak at 1000 level,including retaining his Wimbledon title, heading into the North American hard-court swing, before skipping the event in Canada.The 24-year-old said at the time the decision was taken to “prioritise [his] health”.Sinner’s subsequent withdrawal from Cincinnatifollows that of world No 2 Carlos Alcarazas the Spaniard continues to battle a wrist injury.The Cincinnati Open and Montreal Masters are the two principal warm-up events ahead of the final grand slam of the season, the US Open, which starts in New York on 30 August.Explore more on these topicsJannik SinnerTennisnewsShareReuse this content

title: How Trabzonspor shocked Turkish rivals to make Mohamed Salah their Black Sea saviour | Mohamed Salah | The Guardian
description: Never before has a big name rejected Istanbul, but Trabzonspor, a club on the rise, offered Mohamed Salah more than riches
Author: Emre Sarigul
Headline: Never before has a big name rejected Istanbul, but Trabzonspor, a club on the rise, offered Mohamed Salah more than riches
Content: Mohamed Salah applauds the Trabzonspor fans at his unveiling.Photograph: Ümit Bektaş/ReutersView image in fullscreenMohamed Salah applauds the Trabzonspor fans at his unveiling.Photograph: Ümit Bektaş/ReutersMohamed SalahHow Trabzonspor shocked Turkish rivals to make Mohamed Salah their Black Sea saviourNever before has a big name rejected Istanbul for Trabzon, but former Liverpool striker was offered more than richesEmre Sarigulin IstanbulSun 9 Aug 2026 03.00 EDTLast modified on Sun 9 Aug 2026 21.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleIt began with a text sent during the World Cup. Ertugrul Dogan, the president of Trabzonspor, was watching Egypt when he picked up his phone and messaged his manager, Fatih Tekke. “Coach,” it read. “Do you wantMohamed Salah?”Tekke’s response was immediate enthusiasm, though Trabzonspor’s initial push for Salah went under the radar with Besiktas looking most likely to land the former Liverpool striker. In Turkish football, Istanbul’s Big Three – Galatasaray, Fenerbahce and Besiktas – have long held monopoly on the Super Lig’s marquee signings.Mohamed Salah’s story of success and sacrifice: ‘Chasing a dream I had to reach’Read moreIstanbul is not the capital but it is the undisputed financial, cultural and commercial heartbeat of the country and wider region. It came as a shock, then, whenSalah opted for Trabzonspor.The club are by no means minnows. They form part of the traditional Big Four alongside their Istanbul rivals. Yet the football-crazy port city on the eastern Black Sea coast lacks the cosmopolitan lifestyle Istanbul offers. What it possesses instead is devotion. Most Turkish cities do not have a strong local football identity, with residents supporting one of the major Istanbul sides from afar. Trabzon is one of the few exceptions. The entire region eats, sleeps and breathes for its team.Trabzon is like the Newcastle of Turkey: a proud, working-class city in the north-east with an industrial maritime past, deeply tied to its football club and trying to forge a new identity to adapt to the modern world.Salah’s arrival has thrust a city that often feels politically and geographically sidelined onto the global stage. This transfer is bigger than football. Trabzon wants to revitalise the city as a maritime trade, tourism and logistics hub. The arrival of the Egyptian superstar ensures an even bigger spotlight on the city.View image in fullscreenAn excited Trabzonspor fan decked in traditional claret and sky blue colours sports sunglasses decorated with new signing Mohamed Salah.Photograph: Ümit Bektaş/ReutersThe chaotic scenes at Trabzon airport on Wednesday – when supporters turned the terminal into a sea of red flares, followed by tens of thousands packing Papara Park for Salah’s signing ceremony – demonstrated their fervour.Salah could easily have accepted lucrative proposals in the Saudi Pro League or Major League Soccer, but their fan culture pales by comparison. Crucially, the 34-year-old remains in a highly competitive league in the Uefa zone; Trabzonspor need only navigate the playoff rounds for a place in the Europa League group stage.“I am seeing a reception like this for the first time in my life,” Salah told the roaring crowd during his unveiling. “I came here to win trophies. I am here to bring titles to this club.”Trabzonspor have played the role of disruptors in Turkish football – the Black Sea rebels who broke Istanbul’s stranglehold in the 1970s and most recently won the league title in 2021–22. But never before has a player of this magnitude rejected Istanbul for Trabzon.View image in fullscreenSalah takes a photo as the fans offer a hearty welcome.Photograph: Ümit Bektaş/ReutersThe Turkish top flight is experiencing a renaissance. Leandro Trossard joined Besiktas after a title-winning campaign with Arsenal; Victor Osimhen continues to spearhead Galatasaray’s attack; while Nathan Aké and Mason Greenwood now line up for Fenerbahce. The league is also developing world-class homegrown talent, with Arda Güler at Real Madrid and Ferdi Kadioglu at Brighton serving as prime examples.Trabzonspor’s pursuit of Salah was executed in the shadows. The club deployed their former winger Mahmoud Hassan – known as Trézéguet – as their secret operative. Salah’s international teammate spoke with the Egyptian captain daily, to help convince him to consider the move.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballPreview latestEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionThere was a cultural element, too: moving to a welcoming, Muslim-majority nation where Salah and his family could feel immediately at home. Trabzonspor locked him into a two-year contract through to June 2028 and disclosed the financial details on the Public Disclosure Platform (KAP). Salah will earn a base annual salary of €10m (£8.5m) alongside a guaranteed €7m annual signing bonus, netting him €17m per season (€34m net over two years).Because wages in Turkey are paid net, with the club covering all tax liabilities, Salah in effect takes home 50% more than his final Liverpool contract. The deal also includes performance add-ons, a 5% agent’s fee on gross wages and an extraordinary image-rights agreement granting Salah a 20% royalty on all personal merchandise sold through the club’s official TS Club retail network.The commercial return was immediate. Within 24 hours of Salah landing, Trabzonspor sold more than 17,000 season tickets, generating £11m. Dogan confirmed that total projected revenue from tickets, sponsorships and merchandise during the Salah era is expected to approach £22m, in effect self-funding the transfer.View image in fullscreenTrabzonspor supporters unveil a banner celebrating Salah.Photograph: Nurgul Gunaydin/AFP/Getty ImagesCrucially, Trabzonspor did not overextend themselves. Balanced by roughly €95m raised in player sales since last season, the transfer is manageable financially. Salah joins a side on an upward trajectory under Tekke. Languishing in 13th when Tekke took over in March 2025, the team recovered to finish eight points behind the champions, Galatasaray, in third and won the Turkish Cup.Tekke added the Valencia defender Cenk Özkacar and the Manchester United loanee André Onana in goal and Trabzonspor are in talks with Darwin Núñez.Taking his favoured No 10 shirt, Salah steps into a side in the ascendant. Yet the challenge remains steep. Galatasaray have won four consecutive league titles, while Besiktas and Fenerbahce have spent lavishly this summer. Trabzonspor will be hoping his arrival serves as a catalyst for a change in fortunes.For Trabzon and the eastern region, however, Salah’s arrival is far more than a transfer story. The tide could be turning back in the favour of the Black Sea Storm.Explore more on these topicsMohamed SalahTrabzonsporEuropean club footballfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: Premier League 2026-27 preview No 1: Arsenal | Premier League previews 2026-27 | The Guardian
description: With most of their rivals changing managers, can Arsenal go back-to-back for the first time in more than 90 years?
Author: Ed Aarons
Headline: With most of their rivals changing managers, can Arsenal go back-to-back for the first time in more than 90 years?
Content: Arsenal’s Premier League title parade drew an estimated million-plus people on to the streets of North London. Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The GuardianWith most of their rivals changing managers, can the champions go back-to-back for the first time in more than 90 years?ByEd AaronsSun 9 Aug 2026 19.01 EDTLast modified on Sun 9 Aug 2026 19.02 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleGuardian writers’ predicted position:1st (NB: this is not necessarily Ed Aarons’ prediction but the average of our writers’ tips)Last season’s position:1stProspectsEven losing on penalties inthe Champions League finalcould not take any of the gloss off last season as Arsenalended their 22-year waitto be crowned Premier League champions. The celebrations have continued all summer aftersome wild scenes on the streets of north Londonon their return from Budapest, although concerns over the fitness of some key players after their exploits at the World Cup are mounting.Arsenal have acted quickly to reinforce their midfieldby signing Bruno Guimarãesfrom Newcastle given Declan Rice’s workload must be managed very carefully afterplaying through neural painin his hamstring and lower back since December. Thearrival of Greece forward Christos Tzolisto replace Leandro Trossard also looks like a smart piece of business on the left-hand side of the attack. But withVinícius Junior staying at Real Madrid, despite Arsenal’s best efforts, supporters will be hoping there is still a chance that the sporting director, Andrea Berta, could conjure up a heavyweight attacking signing before the window closes given Bukayo Saka’s fitness problems in recent seasons.The back injury thatwill sideline William Salibafor an unknown period could prove even more central to Arsenal’s hopes of retaining their title. A defence that conceded 27 goals last year in the Premier League may struggle without the immense talents of the France defender, even if they can bring in Ezri Konsa from Aston Villa as hoped. Whether Arsenal can maintaintheir dominance from set piecesover the past two campaigns will also be crucial, with more scrutiny expected from video assistant referees after the fallout from their controversialvictory at West Ham in May.Not since 1935, whenArsenalbecame the second team to win three successive league titles, have they retained their crown. Having strengthened the deepest squad in the division still further, they will take some stopping again.Past five seasonsOff-field pictureMoney definitely isn’t an issue for Stan Kroenke. Arsenal’s co-owner becameAmerica’s largest private landownerthis year and has spent more than £1.5bn on new players since becoming the majority shareholder in 2011 through his holding company, Kroenke Sports & Entertainment (KSE). Next on the agenda isan upgrade to the EmiratesStadiumthat could increase the capacity of their home to more than 70,000. Talks have begun with the stadium’s original architects, Populous, over a project that could cost up to £500m. The much-criticised shirtsleeve deal with Visit Rwanda ended last season and has been replaced by the HR company Deel, itself controversial in some sections of the Arsenal fanbase, while Emirates have renewed their longstanding partnership until 2033.Owner-fan relationshipKroenke and his son Josh – who are co-chairs – clearly revelled in carrying out the Premier League trophy at Selhurst Park before it was presented to the captain, Martin Ødegaard,after Arsenal’s final game of the seasonin May. Having once been criticised for running the club “like an investment vehicle”, now they are praised for the enormous effect they have made.Kroenke Jr’s promisethere would be “no standing still once this season ends” was an ominous sign to their rivals given KSE have a reputation as serial winners in a number of sports in America.The managerMikel Arteta’s expected bumper new contract extension – that will make him one of the best-paid managers in the world – has yet to be confirmed, but there is no doubting his commitment to the cause. The Spaniard could not bear to watch as Manchester City’s challenge collapsed against Bournemouth last season and wasin his back garden “building a fire”when Arsenal were confirmed as champions. With Pep Guardiola gone,Arteta has the opportunityto build a new winning dynasty of his own.Star signingView image in fullscreenThe Gunners fans will be hoping to see Bruno Guimarães’ goal celebration on numerous occasions this season.Photograph: David Price/Arsenal FC/Getty ImagesThe arrival of Guimarães was another big statement of intent from Arsenal. The former Newcastle captain wants to win more trophies after capturing hearts and minds on Tyneside and he will provide several options in the already well-stacked engine room. As well as relieving the load on Rice, the versatile 28-year-old Brazil midfielder is capable of fulfilling a number of roles, from deep-lying playmaker to box-to box destroyer. While it remains to be seen how Arteta chooses to use Guimarães when he also has Martín Zubimendi, Myles Lewis-Skelly, Ødegaard and Mikel Merino at his disposal, his talents will only add to the quality in Arsenal’s squad.Stat attackReferees have been told to pay much more attention to grappling during set-pieces this season so it will be interesting to see if this has any effect on Arsenal. Only three teams in thePremier Leaguehad a better non-penalty expected goal difference than the Gunners had from set plays alone.A graphic showing the six teams who had a positive xG difference for set pieces in the Premier League in 2025-26: Arsenal on 14.11, Brentford on 9.02, Newcastle on 7.83, Man City on 3.12, Brighton on 0.45 and Aston Villa on 0.31.Set for a breakthroughMax Dowman wasa record-breaking revelationas he dipped his toes into senior football for the first time last season and the signs are that the 16-year-old could be handed more opportunities after impressing again during pre-season. A brilliant goal and an assist against Girona capped a man-of-the-match display from the right flank. With Saka and Noni Madueke to be eased back in after returning from World Cup duty, Dowman is ready to add to his solitary Premier League start, against Crystal Palace on the final day of last season, and should appear more regularly in cup competitions.World Cup impactRice and Saka arrived in the United Statesfeeling the effects of a marathon seasonand it was to their immense credit that they played through the pain barrier and made it to England’s eighth match of the tournament. Only Thomas Tuchel knows why he left Saka on the bench in the semi-final against Argentina andhis hat-trick in the third-place playoffa few days later showed how potent he can be even with an achilles problem. Both require an extended break before returning to the rigours of club football and Arsenal will give them as long as possible. But such is their importance that it will be sooner rather than later.Explore more on these topicsPremier League previews 2026-27ArsenalPremier LeaguefeaturesShareReuse this content

title: Seesaw draw in Malaysia gives Xabi Alonso food for thought at Chelsea | Friendlies | The Guardian
description: Chelsea’s 3-3 draw with the Malaysian champions Johor Darul Ta’zim showed Xabi Alonso has problems to solve before the season begins
Author: Sam Cunningham
Headline: Chelsea’s 3-3 draw with the Malaysian champions Johor Darul Ta’zim showed Xabi Alonso has problems to solve before the season begins
Content: Xabi Alonso is confronted by Kevin Medina of JDT during the preseason friendly match.Photograph: Darren Walsh/Chelsea FC/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenXabi Alonso is confronted by Kevin Medina of JDT during the preseason friendly match.Photograph: Darren Walsh/Chelsea FC/Getty ImagesFriendliesSeesaw draw in Malaysia gives Xabi Alonso food for thought at ChelseaDelap scores twice from spot in 3-3 draw with JDTManager made 11 changes against Malaysian championsSam Cunninghamat the Sultan Ibrahim StadiumSun 9 Aug 2026 15.05 EDTLast modified on Sun 9 Aug 2026 21.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleChelsea’s problems mounted as their pre-season tour came to an end in a strangely fiery draw against the Malaysian champions Johor Darul Ta’zim. The omens do not look promising with a bloated choice of forwards, echoes of their inexperience and indiscipline last season, and fewer than two weeks for the new manager,Xabi Alonso, to reintegrate key players and work with the entirety of his squad before they kick off the Premier League season against Fulham – managed by his old friend Álvaro Arbeloa – on 24 August.Alonso, tasked with transforming a club that finished 10th in the Premier League last season into Champions League qualifiers, made 11 changes for the friendly against JDT. He rested players after beating Milan with a strong lineup only 24 hours earlier, 600 miles away.Iraola says Liverpool have work to do as familiar frailties in defence prove costlyRead moreWhile the defence and midfield were packed with teenagers, the front three – Estêvão Willian, Liam Delap and Nicolas Jackson – would be welcomed by most Premier League clubs, having costChelseamore than £100m combined in the past three years.Delap scored twice from the penalty spot – as many goals in 20 minutes as he managed in the entirety of his first season at Chelsea after joining from Ipswich last summer. The 23-year-old is believed to want to stay and fight for his place, having already proved his Premier League pedigree with 12 top-flight goals for Ipswich. Yet Alonso has so many options: João Pedro, one of the standout strikers last season; the new signing Danny Welbeck; and Jackson, who gave the club something to think about on his loan at Bayern Munich last season.Emmanuel Emegha arrived recently from sister club Strasbourg, and may well go out on loan. They also still have Marc Guiu on the books.Mykhailo Mudryk returning unexpectedly early from a drugs ban at the end of July was a curveball, adding to a rich choice of options on the wing including Cole Palmer, Estêvão – looking sharp again on Sunday after an injury that derailed the teenager’s promising first season at Stamford Bridge – and the record signing Morgan Rogers, who frequently played off the left for Aston Villa.Plenty of time remains before the transfer window closes at the end of the month, but Chelsea’s squad stands at a staggering 41 players, with no European football next season and busy weeks of potential disruption ahead that will not ease Alonso’s stresses.View image in fullscreenLiam Delap scores Chelsea’s second penalty of the evening.Photograph: Darren Walsh/Chelsea FC/Getty ImagesThe JDT manager, Xisco Muñoz, was known for his fierce passion and aggressive football at Watford, and his players treated the game against Chelsea like a competitive fixture at the Sultan Ibrahim Stadium in Johor. They flew into challenges, unsettling Chelsea’s players, competing with an intensity rarely seen in a preseason friendly. The visitors failed to keep tempers in check.There were several flashpoints throughout the match. Delap and Jackson were needlessly booked for dissent, arguing with the referee about challenges on teammates. Estêvão was lucky not to be sent off after kicking out when he felt he was denied a penalty – instead shown a yellow card.Geovany Quenda came off the bench and was also booked for launching into an entirely unnecessary challenge, as though settling a score. Sixteen-year-old Reggie Watson was booked in stoppage time, making it five yellow cards.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballPreview latestEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionChelsea received 11 red cards last season – twice as many as any other side and a club record – and Alonso has diverged from the owners’ policy of signing young by adding Welbeck, 35, and Jordan Henderson, 36. The club have not fielded a player over 30 since Thiago Silva, then 39, left in May 2024, but it might take more than a couple of veterans to sort the problem out.JDT took the lead when they caught Chelsea on a break and Arif Aiman – known in these parts as the ‘Asian Messi’ – scored from a rapid move. Delap levelled just before half-time, then gave Chelsea the lead just after the hour. But JDT equalised three minutes later from Óscar Arribas’s heavily deflected free kick, then retook the lead when Bérgson finished into the bottom corner from distance with four minutes remaining. Mudryk, on in the 87th minute, produced the awkward cross that forced Antonio Glauder’s own goal with a minute on the clock, to avoid an embarrassing defeat.Chelsea return to London after a punishing schedule. Their last three games were in three countries over five days: Juventus in Hong Kong, Milan in Indonesia and JDT inMalaysia– the last two in successive days, their plane landing in Malaysia at 3am on the day of the game.Alonso has only two weeks – and one final friendly against Real Sociedad on Saturday – to work with the £117m signing Rogers, the injury-prone captain Reece James and the disgruntled star Enzo Fernández, all due back at the club’s Cobham training ground this week following extended World Cup breaks. Then the season will kick off – and the fun and games will really begin.Explore more on these topicsFriendliesXabi AlonsoChelseaMalaysianewsShareReuse this content

title: José Mourinho reveals he signed contract to succeed Alex Ferguson at Manchester United in 2013 | José Mourinho | The Guardian
description: José Mourinho claims in a new Netflix documentary, backed up by Alex Ferguson, that he signed a deal in 2013 but reneged on it to return to Chelsea
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: José Mourinho claims in a new Netflix documentary, backed up by Alex Ferguson, that he signed a deal in 2013 but reneged on it to return to Chelsea
Content: José Mourinho became Manchester United manager in 2016 but says he had signed a deal to take the job three years earlier.Photograph: Christopher Thomond/The GuardianView image in fullscreenJosé Mourinho became Manchester United manager in 2016 but says he had signed a deal to take the job three years earlier.Photograph: Christopher Thomond/The GuardianJosé MourinhoJosé Mourinho reveals he signed contract to succeed Alex Ferguson at Manchester United in 2013Mourinho: I reneged on deal and returned to ChelseaFerguson confirms story in new Netflix documentaryPA MediaSun 9 Aug 2026 19.24 EDTLast modified on Sun 9 Aug 2026 20.09 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleJosé Mourinho has revealed he signed a contract to succeed Sir Alex Ferguson asManchester Unitedmanager in 2013 only to tearfully renege on the deal and return to Chelsea.The football world was rocked when theScottish great announced he was retiringhaving overseen a 13th Premier League title triumph during a spell of unrivalled dominance at Old Trafford.The five big beasts are gone: who will be the Premier League’s next alpha manager? | Jonathan WilsonRead moreUnited have failed to return to the top of the English game since Ferguson stepped down, withhis successor, David Moyes, sackedafter only 10 months in charge.Mourinho was later brought in, spending two and a half years in charge from 2016, but revealed in a new Netflix documentary about his life that he had agreed to come earlier.“I go to Chelsea in 2013 but in that period there is something nobody knows,” the Portuguese said in the documentary, which is entitled Mourinho. “I think I can say because I don’t hurt anyone with the truth, and I think the objective of this work that we are doing is to tell the truth. When I leftReal Madrid, I signed with Manchester United to go to Manchester United after Sir Alex.”Mourinho continued: “I was, of course, very flattered, because Manchester United has an incredible appeal. When I say Real Madrid is the biggest club in the world, I have to say that Manchester United is very, very close.double quotation markHe phoned me and he was crying. He says: ‘Alex, I can’t take it – I’ve given my word to Chelsea.’Sir Alex Ferguson“But one thing is love for football, and another thing is love for a certain club. I think this is more powerful than love for football and, fundamentally, after Real Madrid, I needed to feel that I’m loved.”Ferguson was one of the footballing figures interviewed for the new documentary and admits he was under the illusion Mourinho was accepting the offer, only for the situation to change in a matter of hours.“Early evening he phoned me and he was crying,” the United great said. “And he says: ‘Alex, I can’t take it – I’ve given my word toChelsea, and I’m not going to break my word.’ The reason he gave to me I could understand, but I was disappointed.”Mourinho had a strong bond with Chelsea after leading them to two Premier League titles, an FA Cup and two League Cups during his first spell.View image in fullscreenAlex Ferguson’s long spell as Manchester United manager ended in May 2013.Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The GuardianThe Portuguese parked differences with the Chelsea owner, Roman Abramovich, to return to Stamford Bridge after leaving Real Madrid, winning another league crown and League Cup before being sacked in December 2015.“For me to lose the chance to be the coach to succeed Sir Alex Ferguson was dramatic, but I don’t regret because it was a decision that I made with my heart,” Mourinho, now back in charge of Real Madrid, said.“And I think it is nature that says something that when you do something for love, you are never doing anything wrong. I think it’s nature. I did it for love.“I went back with the feeling of, yes, I go home, but with big responsibility because what I did before is history, and you don’t want to destroy your legacy.”Explore more on these topicsJosé MourinhoManchester UnitedReal MadridChelseanewsShareReuse this content

title: Transfer roundup: Digne returns to PSG from Villa, Fulham agree £30m deal for Charles | Transfer window | The Guardian
description: Lucas Digne has returned to PSG on a three-year contract while Northern Ireland international Shea Charles is expected to sign five-year deal with Fulham
Author: Paul MacInnes
Headline: Lucas Digne has returned to PSG on a three-year contract while Northern Ireland international Shea Charles is expected to sign five-year deal with Fulham
Content: Lucas Digne returns to PSG having first featured for them from 2013-16.Photograph: Jacob King/PAView image in fullscreenLucas Digne returns to PSG having first featured for them from 2013-16.Photograph: Jacob King/PATransfer windowTransfer roundup: Digne returns to PSG from Villa, Fulham agree £30m deal for CharlesFrance full-back Lucas Digne signs three-year PSG dealMidfielder Shea Charles to sign five-year Fulham contractPaul MacInnes,Guardian sportand agenciesSun 9 Aug 2026 18.07 EDTFirst published on Sun 9 Aug 2026 17.14 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleFrance defender Lucas Digne has completed his return to Paris Saint-Germain from Aston Villa on a three-year contract.The 33-year-old full-back, who featured in six ofLes Bleus’ World Cup matches this summer, had two years left on his contract with the Midlands club, with PSG triggering a reported release clause of between £6m-£7m.Bruno Guimarães completes £75m Arsenal move: ‘I needed a new challenge’Read moreVilla confirmed Digne’s exit on their website, adding that he is “a consummate professional, who was highly regarded by his fellow players and staff alike”.He made 182 appearances in all competitions for Villa, scoring four goals and making 24 assists, after joining from Everton in a £25m deal in January 2022. He played a key role for Unai Emery’s side as they won the Europa League last season.The Frenchman made 30 Ligue 1 appearances in a three-year spell at PSG until 2016, when he moved on to Barcelona. He told PSG’s website: “I am very honoured to be returning to Paris Saint-Germain following the wonderful experience I had here more than 10 years ago.”Fulhamhave sought to bolster their midfield by spending £30m on Southampton’s Shea Charles.Charles, a Northern Ireland international and breakout star of the last Championship season, is expected to sign a five-year deal at Craven Cottage once a medical assessment and legal formalities are completed.View image in fullscreenShea Charles was a breakout star in the Championship last season, helping Southampton to reach the playoffs.Photograph: Matt Watson/Southampton FC/Getty ImagesFulham will pay an initial fee of £26m, with another £4m dependent on performance, with the size of the fee believed to have ultimately deterred alternative interest from Leeds.The 22-year-old played 2,000 minutes in the Championship last season as Southampton reached the playoffs before being excluded following revelations of spying against opponents. At Fulham, Charles will be expected to act as the linchpin of the midfield following the sale of Sasa Lukic to Ipswich earlier in the weekend.Charles joins the young forwards Jonah Kusi-Asare and Gonzalo García as well as 21-year-old attacking midfielder César Palacios on the list of summer signings as Fulham seek to reduce the average age of their squad following the switch of manager from Marco Silva to the former Real Madrid B team coach Álvaro Arbeloa.Trevoh Chalobah’s move toComofrom Chelsea has been confirmed, in a deal worth an initial £25.7m. Terms for a five-year contract were agreed last week, but as the move was announced on Sunday, the England defender said he was “thrilled and honoured” to be joining Cesc Fàbregas’s side.The pair overlapped at Stamford Bridge towards the end of the Spaniard’s time playing in England, and Chalobah said: “It’s an ambitious, rising project, and working with Cesc Fàbregas again is truly special. I can’t wait to bring my experience to the team, feel the incredible atmosphere at the stadium, and connect with the fans.”skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballPreview latestEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionFàbregas said: “Trevoh is a leader who can raise the level of the team, and I am very happy that he has chosen Como.”Gustavo Hamer has completed a move from the Championship, this time renewing his relationship withCoventryafter leaving Sheffield United for a fee of £6m plus add-ons. The Brazilian-born talent will become the Sky Blues’ sixth signing since returning to the top flight, with two big-ticket deals, £24m goalkeeper Carl Rushworth and £25m Ghanaian international midfielder Caleb Yirenkyi, joining in the last week alone.View image in fullscreenTrevoh Chalobah will be linking up Cesc Fàbregas after joining Como on a five-year dealPhotograph: Nick Potts/PAHamer was a key part of Mark Robins’s Coventry side as they reached the FA Cup semi-final and Championship playoff final two years ago, only for the attacking midfielder to then leave the club in a £15m deal with the promoted Blades. Following immediate relegation and a misfiring season last term, Hamer will begin a second stint at the CBS Arena, this time under Frank Lampard.Midfielder Idrissa Gueye has joined Saudi Pro League newcomersDiriyah. The 36-year-old left Everton at the end of last season and arrives at his new club as a free agent. Gueye played in all four of Senegal’s matches at this summer’s World Cup as his country progressed to the last 32.Elsewhere,Hullcompleted the signing of the Swedish wing-back Elliot Stroud from Mjallby. The 24-year-old featured in every game for his country at the World Cup and has signed a four-year deal. Reports also continue to link Sporting’s centre-half Ousmane Diomande with a £30m move toNottingham Forest, with the Ivorian international said to be travelling to the UK from Portugal on Sunday in order to complete his medical. Diomande is understood to be the new Forest manager Oliver Glasner’s first-choice signing, and a player seen as having a key role to play in the German’s preferred 3-4-3 setup.Explore more on these topicsTransfer windowFulhamCoventry CityNottingham ForestnewsShareReuse this content

title: Hibernian stun Rangers at Ibrox while O’Neill misses Høgh treble in Celtic win | Scottish Premiership | The Guardian
description: Callum Wright scored an injury-time winner as Hibernian beat Rangers 2-1 while Celtic won 5-1 at Kilmarnock despite manager Martin O’Neill missing the game
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Callum Wright scored an injury-time winner as Hibernian beat Rangers 2-1 while Celtic won 5-1 at Kilmarnock despite manager Martin O’Neill missing the game
Content: Hibernian players and fans show their delight after Callum Wright’s winner.Photograph: Steve Welsh/PAView image in fullscreenHibernian players and fans show their delight after Callum Wright’s winner.Photograph: Steve Welsh/PAScottish PremiershipHibernian stun Rangers at Ibrox while O’Neill misses Høgh treble in Celtic winCallum Wright scores injury-time winner for visitorsMartin O’Neill absent from Rugby Park after operationPA MediaSun 9 Aug 2026 13.30 EDTFirst published on Sun 9 Aug 2026 11.04 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleDerek McInnes suffered a damaging home debut asRangersmanager with a 2-1 Premiership defeat toHiberniancompounded by striker Youssef Chermiti being carried off the pitch on a stretcher.David Gray’s side took the lead in the 12th minute with a Josh Campbell penalty after the video assistant referee (VAR) had flagged up that Vanja Dragojevic, making his firstRangersstart after signing from Partizan Belgrade, had fouled Jason Kerr in the area.There was more woe before the break when Chermiti, subject to a failed bid by Galatasaray for a reported club record fee of £22million, having to go off after picking up an injury.Rangers pushed forward relentlessly and were rewarded in the 85th minute when the Hibs defender Miguel Chaiwa turned the ball past the goalkeeper Raphael Sallinger.However, in the third minute of added time, the substitute Callum Wright guided a shot into the far corner for a stunning win.With Celtic andSt Mirrenboth on six points from two games, Rangers are five behind with McInnes looking for his first win after three matches in the Ibrox hot seat.Kasper Høgh scored a hat-trick, his first goals forCeltic, as the Scottish champions made light of the absence of their manager Martin O’Neill with a 5-1 win atKilmarnock. O’Neill missed the trip to Rugby Park after what the club had said earlier this week was a “small procedure” in hospital.No details were given about O’Neill’s operation, which came after the veteran Northern Irish manager took charge ofCeltic’s win against Dundeein their first game of the season. But the club’s assistant manager, Shaun Maloney, speaking before Sunday’s kick-off, said O’Neill was on the mend. “He is doing better again,” Maloney told Sky Sports. “He came to the team hotel and spoke to the players but he just needs an extra few days.”View image in fullscreenCeltic’s Kasper Høgh scores the first of his three goals against Kilmarnock.Photograph: Robert Perry/PAO’Neill’s mood would doubtless have been improved by the performance of his side, withCeltic3-0 ahead before half-time thanks to Høgh. The Danish striker, who joined in July from Bodø/Glimt, needed less than a minute to score his first Celtic goal, heading in at the back post from a cross by Arne Engels.Høgh doubled Celtic’s lead in the 33rd minute, with Camilo Durán seizing on Johnly Yfeko’s pass out of defence. He combined with Benjamin Nygren to work the ball to Høgh on the left edge of the box, with the forward finishing well.Two minutes later, Høgh had his hat-trick. Nygren slipping the ball right for Durán, whose cross took the Kilmarnock goalkeeper Max Stryjek out of play, with Høgh nodding into an empty net.Celtic extended their lead early in the second half after they were effectively gifted a fourth goal by Stryjek. His pass out of defence went straight to Nygren in front of goal and his shot into the top corner made it 4-0.Michael Schjønning-Larsen pulled a goal back for Kilmarnock in the 56th minute after finishing a well-worked move. But Celtic went four goals ahead again when Luke McCowan, moments after coming on, volleyed in from close range 15 minutes from time after Kilmarnock made a mess of trying to clear the ball from a corner.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballPreview latestEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionView image in fullscreenCeltic’s assistant manager Shaun Maloney took charge with Martin O’Neill still recovering from a procedure in hospital.Photograph: Robert Perry/PAThreeHeartssummer signings were on target as Wouter Vrancken belatedly got his reign up and running with a 4-0 win overDundee United. The Belgian had suffered four consecutive defeats – three in Europe – since replacing Derek McInnes in June, but his new-look team tore United apart in their first home league game of the season.Tom Renaud, Calvin Miller and Josh McPake all marked their first league outings at Tynecastle with goals, while last season’s talisman Cláudio Braga broke his duck for the campaign.Hearts made a fast start as Renaud, a few days after notching against Benfica, unleashed a ferocious strike beyond Jack Walton from just short of 30 yards after being teed up by Braga in the fourth minute.View image in fullscreenJosh McPake turns away after scoring Hearts’ fourth goal against Dundee United.Photograph: Malcolm Mackenzie/Getty ImagesThe home side were gifted the chance to double their lead when VAR spotted Daniel Bennie wrestling Jamie McCart to the ground in the box. Miller stepped up to fire the penalty straight down the middle.Hearts killed off any hopes of a United fightback in the 56th minute when Braga drilled in a low angled shot from 12 yards out after being set up by Sabah Kerjota. McPake then marked his first competitive start for Hearts with his first goal as he tucked a clinical low finish beyond Walton after playing a one-two with Braga on the left of the box.In Sunday’s other 3pm kick-off,Motherwelldrew 0-0 at home toFalkirk.On Saturday,DundeebeatAberdeen2-0 thanks to goals from Joe Westley and Joe Bevan whileSt MirrenedgedSt Johnstone1-0 courtesy of Killian Phillips’ penalty.Explore more on these topicsScottish PremiershipRangersHibernianKilmarnockCelticHeartsDundee UnitednewsShareReuse this content

title: Alexia Putellas: ‘I’m hungry to win, to fight with my teammates for victory’ | London City Lionesses | The Guardian
description: London City Lionesses’ headline signing tells Tom Garry about expectations, the lure of playing in England and the prospect of being kicked by her former teammates
Author: Tom Garry
Headline: London City Lionesses’ headline signing tells Tom Garry about expectations, the lure of playing in England and the prospect of being kicked by her former teammates
Content: Alexia Putellas will be the first Ballon d’Or winner to play in the WSL.Photograph: London City LionessesView image in fullscreenAlexia Putellas will be the first Ballon d’Or winner to play in the WSL.Photograph: London City LionessesLondon City LionessesInterviewAlexia Putellas: ‘I’m hungry to win, to fight with my teammates for victory’Tom GarryLondon City Lionesses’ headline signing talks expectations, the lure of playing in England and the prospect of being kicked by her former teammatesSun 9 Aug 2026 04.00 EDTLast modified on Sun 9 Aug 2026 21.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleMomentarily, Alexia Putellas appears somewhat nervous, stepping inside the cramped conference room in a Kent hotel to see 23 reporters squeezed inside, all eager to hear fromthe Women’s Super League’s newest global superstar, but she quickly composes herself. Within minutes, she is into her stride, asking for tips about roast dinners and drawing laughs from the room as she jokes that her friends who play for other English clubs have told her they are going to kick her. Welcome to the WSL.Alessia Russo: ‘When you join the club, you take on a part of Arsenal and the love’Read moreSpeaking in English throughout the 20-minute session with ever-increasing proficiency, the two-time Ballon d’Or winner and four-time Champions League winner explains why she has swapped the prestige of Barcelona – where she has been idolised over a trophy-laden 14-year spell – fora team that finished 22 points adriftof the European qualification places last term.Backed by the ambitious businesswoman Michele Kang, the independently run London City Lionesses have made eye-catching, world-class signings this summer, includingthe France forward Kadidiatou Dianifrom Lyonnes – who arealso majority-ownedby Kang – Putellas’sBarcelona teammate Mapi Leónandthe former England goalkeeper Mary Earpsfrom PSG.Undoubtedly, though, Putellas is the biggest of them all and the signing that will have made all of women’s football take notice. As a serial winner will Putellas have to be patient for trophies here?“Both can live together, my mentality and the moment of the project. I’m going to bring to the project whatever the project needs from me, so I’m 100% committed,”the 2023 World Cup winnersays. “I’m hungry to win, to be better day after day, to fight with my teammates for the victory. I’m going to try to give my best to the team and let’s see at the end of the season how good we were.”View image in fullscreenBarcelona made Putellas a parting gift of a photo of herself surrounded by every trophy she’d won while at the club.Photograph: Albert Gea/ReutersLondon City Lionesses werepromoted to the WSL in 2025, finished sixth last season in their top-flight debut and are yet to win a major trophy. Asked what her expectations are, Putellas says: “I don’t have expectations. I just want the hard work we are doing to speak for itself. It’s a hard competition. Of course, I have a competitive mind and I want to win every game. But I don’t have expectations in this sport. In my opinion, you shouldn’t. Just work in the back[ground] and give everything.”Putellas was named as the Women’s Champions League’s player of the season after helping fireBarcelona to a fourth European title in six seasons, yet at the age of 32, she still feels she can improve – “Of course, always, day after day, I want to learn things [and] just keep going, I never stop [trying to] be as good as I can,” – but specifically she thinks the WSL can add elements to her skillset.“It will be different, but that’s why I’m here, because I’m looking forward to improving myself,” she says. “It’s being a more complete player, as much as I can. It’s about learning new things, playing with and against other players and just trying to find where my limits are. It will take time because it’s a new beginning and a big change for me.View image in fullscreenAlexia Putellas will be hoping to stamp her name on more than just her contract and the camera after joining London City Lionesses.Photograph: London City Lionesses“[In the WSL] you never know what will be the result of the game; it’s a very competitive league, week after week. I imagine all the games will push you to your limits. It’s a very entertaining league.“The first conversation [I had with London City] was about what the club wants and how ambitious the project is. I want to be part of that journey, bring the experience I have and learn as a player and make me more complete. I made the move for that and just being in other positions that I’ve never been in. In my opinion, this league can give me that.”When asked if she had sought advice from her former Barcelona teammates, such as the England duo Keira Walsh and Lucy Bronze, about what to expect in England, she says: “Well, some of them told me that it’s a hard league and they’re going to kick me. No, I’m just joking.”skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toMoving the GoalpostsNo topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s footballPreview latestEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionShe also chuckled when asked about London’s traffic and expensive property prices, even if she was slightly hesitant reflecting on her first taste of an English fry-up: “Erm, yes. It was quite different. Not the beans, but the sausages and eggs. It was fine.”View image in fullscreenAlexia Putellas scored twice when Spain thrashed England 4-0 in June, ending the Lionesses’ chances of automatic World Cup qualification.Photograph: Francisco Ubilla/ReutersShe will have plenty of help when it comes to settling into the London City, with six Spanish teammates anda head coach, Eder Maestre, who she says did a “really good job with Tenerife”. Maestre, yet anothercoaching export of the Basque Country, was at Tenerife for a year and a half, finishing sixth in his only full season and taking them to fifth by the time he left for England.Putellas knows there will be differences tactically in the English game and thinks that can help her add even more strings to her bow.“I really believe that moving to England can give me something more,” she says. “Like, I can control the low blocks and all this stuff; I am used to it playing in Spain. I have already controlled that, so [I want] different kind of games or box-to-box and all this stuff.”She then apologises for her English – not that any apology was needed – and explains she is still learning the language and working hard to improve it all the time. If her footballing ability continues to enhance too, then WSL defenders had better beware.Explore more on these topicsLondon City LionessesSpain women's football teamWomen's Super LeagueWomen's footballinterviewsShareReuse this content

title: Hodgkinson believes gold at home European Championships ‘would mean almost as much as Olympics’ | European Athletics Championships | The Guardian
description: Keely Hodgkinson is the headline act as Birmingham hosts and she believes her 800m clash with Audrey Werro is set to be ‘race of the championships’
Author: Sean Ingle
Headline: Keely Hodgkinson is the headline act as Birmingham hosts and she believes her 800m clash with Audrey Werro is set to be ‘race of the championships’
Content: Keely Hodgkinson believes standards in the women’s 800m are high in Europe, which adds additional cachet to the European title.Photograph: Dylan Martinez/ReutersView image in fullscreenKeely Hodgkinson believes standards in the women’s 800m are high in Europe, which adds additional cachet to the European title.Photograph: Dylan Martinez/ReutersEuropean Athletics ChampionshipsHodgkinson believes gold at home European Championships ‘would mean almost as much as Olympics’British 800m star is headline act as Birmingham hostsAudrey Werro clash to be ‘race of the championships’Sean IngleSun 9 Aug 2026 15.00 EDTLast modified on Sun 9 Aug 2026 21.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleKeely Hodgkinson says winning a European gold medal in front of her home fans in Birmingham this week will be nearly as special as her Olympic title in Paris.Hodgkinson is the headline act as the EuropeanAthleticsChampion­ships come to Britain for the first time in its 92-year history, but she insists the intense spotlight on her only increases her determination to win 800m gold.Georgia Hunter Bell: ‘Getting the tube to work I was like … oh my God, I’ve kind of messed up my life’Read more“I don’t really see it as pressure,” the 24-year-old said. “I just see it as more of a motivation. There’s going to be a lot of my family there to support me, and hopefully I’ll be able to stand on top of the podium and have a national anthem in the UK. That would be incredibly special. It would mean as much to me, almost, as winning in Paris.”Part of Hodgkinson’s ­excitement comes from knowing that the world’s four ­fastest women in 2026 will all be competing ­including the Swiss star Audrey Werro, who shocked her in June by running 1min 53.98sec, ­making her the third fastest woman in the race’s history.Hodgkinson, though, believes she is still the best in the world over two laps, and intends to prove it against a field that includes the ­former 400m hurdle world ­champion Femke ­Broeders‑Bol, who has run 1:55 this year.Quick GuideEuropean Athletics Championship: day-by-day guideShowMonday 10 AugustAmy Hunt is a warm favourite for the women’s 100m (9.50pm), but no British athlete has won more European golds than DIna Asher-Smith, the defending champion. Elsewhere, Norwegian superstar Jakob Ingebrigtsen returns from an Achilles injury in the men’s 5,000m (8.40pm) and there’s also an intriguing 4x400m mixed relay final (9.40pm).Tuesday 11 AugustKeely Hodgkinson begins the defence of her women’s 800m title (12.05pm). The big event of the night is the men’s 100m, where Italian Marcel Jacobs is the favourite to defend his crown (9.45pm), with Britain’s Romell Glave his closest challenger. The women’s 110m hurdles (9.30pm) should also be a cracker.Wednesday 12 AugustLocal lad Matt Hudson-Smith is expected to win the men’s 400m gold for a third time (8.50pm), while Emily Newnham should medal in the women’s 400m hurdles (9.08pm), although Slovakia’s Emma Zapletalova is the wide-margin favourite.Thursday, 13 AugustHodgkinson goes  in the women’s 800m semi-finals (12:10pm). A stacked evening card includes a men’s 800m final (9.28pm) where Max Burgin and Ben Pattison should feature and the women’s 200m where Hunt (9.50pm) will be favourite. In the women’s steeplechase (8.30pm), Britain’s Elise Thorner should cap a breakout season with gold.Friday 14 AugustAll eyes will be on the women’s 800m final (9.45pm), which could be the race of the year. In June Swiss star Audrey Werro ran the third fastest time in history to beat Hodgkinson in Stockholm. Can the Brit get her revenge? Former 400m hurdles world champion Femke Broeders-Bol is a live threat too. Elsewhere Karsten Warholm should win another men’s 400m hurdles (8.40pm).Saturday, 15 AugustNafi Thiam’s withdrawal with injury means there will be a new heptathlon champion for the first time since 2016 and Katarina Johnson-Thompson will hope to take advantage (7.45pm). Britain also have medal chances in the men’s and women's 4x100m relay (9.33 and 9.48pm), a strong men’s 1500m featuring Jake Wightman (9.07pm) and the women’s 400m (8.10pm) where Amber Anning should medal.Sunday, 16 AugustBritain will expect a bumper day with Georgia Hunter Bell favourite in the women’s 1500m (9.13pm), along with strong medal chances in the women's and men’s 4x400m relay (9.33pm and 9.48pm) and the mixed 4x100m relay (8.35pm). Early birds can catch the women’s and men’s marathon (7:30am and 8:10am), while Mondo Duplantis will hope to get his season back on track with gold in the men’s pole vault (7.30pm)Was this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.“This is what I train for,” ­Hodgkinson said.“This is the ­exciting moment. I’ve had lots of people come around and challenge me but I’ve medalled at every single championships.“It’s going to be the race of the championships. It’s really ­interesting to look at how the standard in Europe has come on. But I think it’s really exciting – it just means that a European title is just as important, and just as fun, as a world title at this point.”Hodgkinson confirmed she was back at full fitness after injuring both knees in a fall on to a metal grate in late June. “I feel in a good place. ­Obviously there’s a bit of a tough patch in June/July but I’m happy and I’m excited to compete and I just think it’ll bring out the best in me.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toSport in FocusOur picture editors select their favourite sporting images from the past week, from the spectacular to the powerful, and with a little bit of fun thrown inPreview latestEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotion“My knees are healed. I’ve got some fat scars but they’re all fine. It was just a sticky one. I didn’t miss any training or anything. It was more just a lot of pain and inflammation. I’m looking forward to putting that behind me.”Britain will hope to get off to a strong start to the championships on Monday, with Amy Hunt the ­favourite for gold in the women’s 100m, ahead of the defending champion Dina Asher-Smith and the Polish star Ewa Swoboda.Hodgkinson, whose 800m campaign begins on Tuesday, with the semi-finals on Thursday and final on Friday, is backing Britain to challenge for the top of the medal table. “I think we’ll get a few surprise medals as well. The team is really strong and I think it’s going to do great things for the sport by ­inspiring the next generation.”Explore more on these topicsEuropean Athletics ChampionshipsKeely HodgkinsonAthleticsnewsShareReuse this content

title: Arteta expects Guimarães to ‘ignite’ Arsenal and help take team to new level | Friendlies | The Guardian
description: Mikel Arteta praised Arsenal’s new signing Bruno Guimarães after watching his side lose 3-2 in the Emirates Cup to Borussia Dortmund
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Mikel Arteta praised Arsenal’s new signing Bruno Guimarães after watching his side lose 3-2 in the Emirates Cup to Borussia Dortmund
Content: Bruno Guimarães is presented to the Arsenal fans before the Emirates Cup match against Borussia Dortmund.Photograph: Jacques Feeney/Offside/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenBruno Guimarães is presented to the Arsenal fans before the Emirates Cup match against Borussia Dortmund.Photograph: Jacques Feeney/Offside/Getty ImagesFriendliesArteta expects Guimarães to ‘ignite’ Arsenal and help take team to new levelArsenal lose 3-2 to Borussia Dortmund in Emirates CupMan City’s wide players shine in 3-2 win against AtléticoPA MediaSun 9 Aug 2026 14.46 EDTLast modified on Sun 9 Aug 2026 20.17 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThe Arsenal manager, Mikel Arteta, has backed “warrior” Bruno Guimarães to “ignite something different” in the Premier League champions. The Brazil midfielder was introduced to fans ahead of Sunday’s 3-2 defeat byBorussia Dortmundin the Emirates Cup after completing his £75m move from Newcastle.The 28-year-old,who has signed a four-year deal, bolsters a midfield which already includes Declan Rice, Martin Ødegaard, Mikel Merino, Martín Zubimendi and Eberechi Eze.Iraola says Liverpool have work to do as familiar frailties in defence prove costlyRead more“You can see the immediate reaction,” Arteta told the club website after Guimarães was given a warm reception by supporters. “I think he describes himself as a warrior. I think he’s a warrior with a tremendous quality as well, and intuition and leadership and charisma that is going to help us. That is going to really ignite something different in the team. I think he’s going to push everybody inside the team as well and that’s the type of player that we need.”After finishing runners-up for three successive seasons,Arsenalended their 22-year wait for the Premier League title last term, in addition to reaching the Champions League and Carabao Cup finals. Guimarães watched on against Dortmund as an Ethan Nwaneri strike and a Viktor Gyökeres penalty were not enough to prevent defeat.Samuele Inácio, Konstantinos Karetsas and Joane Gadou scored for the Bundesliga side at the Emirates Stadium, before Arsenal won a pre-arranged penalty shootout 5-4.“Disappointed that we lost the game,” said Arteta, who gave Ødegaard his first minutes of pre-season following the World Cup and will welcome back his full squad on Monday. “I think there were some poor moments where we were not very recognisable, especially in set-pieces and defending actions and timings that we are normally very efficient [in].“Some other very, very positive attacking combinations, big chances that didn’t finish in anything because of the final pass because they were completely open. But, overall, disappointed because you want to win the games in any context and today, we haven’t managed to do that.”View image in fullscreenManchester City’s Phil Foden falls in a collision with Atlético Madrid’s Morten Hjulmand.Photograph: Greg Baker/AFP/Getty ImagesThe Manchester City manager, Enzo Maresca, praised the impact of his wide players after Antoine Semenyo supplied ⁠assists for Omar Marmoush in a 3-1 victory overAtlético Madridto wrap up their preseason tour ⁠of Asia.Marmoush scored ⁠twice in ​the space of three minutes early in the second half before substitute Rayan Aït-Nouri added a third in stoppage ⁠time, helping City overturn a half-time deficit in front of more than 50,000 fans at Seoul World Cup Stadium.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballPreview latestEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotion“Overall, it was a ⁠very good test against one of the best teams in Europe,” Maresca said. “Credit ​to the players for the effort ‌they have done. From ‌tomorrow pre-season is finished and the real business starts.”Semenyo finished the Asia tour with four assists in ​three matches, while Savinho also impressed on the opposite flank. Aït-Nouri completed the scoring late on, but Maresca said City still needed greater efficiency in front of goal.“We need to be clinical. It’s something we need to improve,” he said. “Slowly we ⁠are getting there and with Erling (Haaland) we can be even more ​dangerous. Today Omar ​scored twice. This is a ​boost.”Maresca said he was encouraged by the progress made during ​his first three ‌matches in charge ​after succeeding Pep ​Guardiola, with City ending their Asia tour with a draw against Inter, before a penalty shootout defeat, and victories over a K League All-Stars side and Atlético.Explore more on these topicsFriendliesArsenalBorussia DortmundManchester CityAtlético MadridnewsShareReuse this content

title: AI push is putting banks at mercy of tech firms, warns Moody’s | Banking | The Guardian
description: Finance sector will gain from the tech but it will need substantial investment and create risks, says rating agency
Author: Kalyeena Makortoff
Headline: Finance sector will gain from the tech but it will need substantial investment and create risks, says rating agency
Content: The reliance of most financial firms on a small set of AI and cloud computing providers risks creating a systemic dependency.Photograph: Ahn Young-joon/APView image in fullscreenThe reliance of most financial firms on a small set of AI and cloud computing providers risks creating a systemic dependency.Photograph: Ahn Young-joon/APBankingAI push is putting banks at mercy of tech firms, warns Moody’sFinance sector will gain from the tech but it will need substantial investment and create risks, says rating agencyKalyeena MakortoffBanking correspondentSun 9 Aug 2026 05.00 EDTLast modified on Sun 9 Aug 2026 21.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThe rating agency Moody’s has said the race to adopt AI is putting big banks at the mercy of a small group of Silicon Valley firms, leaving them vulnerable to widespread outages and price gouging by profit-hungry tech bosses.The financial sector’s efforts to integrate AI into day-to-day operations will eventually cut costs and increase revenues across the City and Wall Street, Moody’s said.But that will require “substantial investments”, and with so many rivals racing towards the same goal, many of those benefits will end up being “competed away”.AI will also create bigger risks around data privacy, cybersecurity, fraud and so-called “deposit flight”, as well as an overdependence on a small number of tech firms, the rating agency warned.That will raise concerns for bosses across the financial sector.More than 75%of City companies now use AI, according to a UK Treasury select committee report published in January, with insurers and international banks among the biggest adopters. They are mostly using it to automate administrative tasks or even help with core operations, including processing insurance claims and assessing customers’ creditworthiness.“The reliance of most financial firms on a relatively small set of foundation AI model and cloud computing providers risks creating a systemic dependency,” the Moody’s report said.“This is because a model outage at one major provider could potentially spread quickly across customers and sectors. As AI adoption deepens, regulators may increase their focus on operational resilience and third-party concentration in the AI model stack.”The AI race also risked creating “vendor dependence risk”, Moody’s said, meaning that “a set of dominant AI model and infrastructure providers could, over time, exert control over the price of AI services”. That issue is likely to emerge as the bosses of loss-making generative AI companies, including the ChatGPT creator OpenAI and the Claude owner Anthropic, come under pressure to deliver profits for investors.“While this could pose credit risks to financial firms, they would nevertheless retain control over key assets, including proprietary data,” Moody’s said. Many big banks and insurers also have longstanding experience negotiating down tech contracts, and may be using open-source AI models, and striking key partnerships, to try to offset “dependency risks”.Lloyds Banking Group’s chief executive, Charlie Nunn, recentlydoubled downon AI investment plans with a £13bn strategy that would involve using the technology to lure new business, improve efficiency and increase payouts for shareholders.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toBusiness TodayGet set for the working day – we'll point you to all the business news and analysis you need every morningPreview latestEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionThat will involve £2bn of cost cuts, which Nunn said would affect staff. “That is going to impact work. It is going to require us to continue to reskill peopleand hire new people, but that’s been my history for 30-odd years in financial services.”Moody’s acknowledged the potential blow to some staff, who could be deemed replaceable as a result of new tech. Its report said there was a 20% chance that, by 2030, AI will be able to do the work of a “solid mid-level employee”.For banks, AI might also make it easier for customers to switch to accounts offering higher interest rates, creating the possibility that large chunks of cash could be moved at short notice. “In this context, depositors’ trust in the institution and the resilience and stability of deposit funding are critical,” Moody’s said.Explore more on these topicsBankingTechnology sectorAI (artificial intelligence)newsShareReuse this content

title: ‘I’ve definitely lost followers’: influencers face backlash over Meta ‘pervert glasses’ content | Meta | The Guardian
description: Using ‘spy glasses’ made by Facebook owner leads to floods of negative comments, say content creators
Author: Sammy Gecsoyler
Headline: Using ‘spy glasses’ made by Facebook owner leads to floods of negative comments, say content creators
Content: Meta’s tech has prompted concerns about privacy and surveillance.Photograph: Carlos Barría/ReutersView image in fullscreenMeta’s tech has prompted concerns about privacy and surveillance.Photograph: Carlos Barría/ReutersMeta‘I’ve definitely lost followers’: influencers face backlash over Meta ‘pervert glasses’ contentUsing ‘spy glasses’ made by Facebook owner leads to floods of negative comments, say content creatorsSammy GecsoylerSun 9 Aug 2026 09.37 EDTLast modified on Sun 9 Aug 2026 21.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleIt was hardly an offensive video. Amid the buzz of the Tour de France finale, Oliver Hooson filmed himself whipping up a delicious-looking flat white for a fellow cycling enthusiast. But after posting the footage on social media, the comments that soon rolled in were a real shock. “PERV,” read one. “Out here pushing creep glasses,” said another. His mistake? Documenting the moment with Meta’s “spy glasses”.Despite being marketed as the latest must-have gadget, Meta’s smartglasses, which can record video footage while being worn, have faced a vicious backlash, particularly relating to concerns about surveillance. There are widespread fears about the glasses being used to film people, especially women, without their consent, and the resultant footage being posted on social media. This has earned them the label of “pervert glasses”, and content creators, no matter how they are used, have faced a flood of negative comments for deploying them.View image in fullscreenOliver HoosonThings reached a peak this summer when Kylie Jenner collaborated with Meta to launch a pair, leading to a flurry of influencers showing off their trendy, Kardashian-approved goggles. Some content creators have been forced to apologise for plugging the specs. Rida Tharana, a content creator with 1.6 million followers on Instagram,“took accountability”for taking part in a Meta campaign to promote the glasses, criticising men who misuse them to “record and harass women”. Self-described pickup artists have used the glasses to film themselves trying to chat up women in public without their knowledge, sometimes making disparaging, misogynistic comments afterwards.Hooson says that, while some of the comments lefton his videowere “savage”, he is fully in support of their message. “It definitely caught me off guard. It was a real ignorant move,” he says, adding that he hates that the glasses are being used against “women mainly being filmed against their knowledge”. The backlash was even coming from those close to home. “Funnily enough, my wife predicted it. She was going to post a banterous comment in a similar tone to the others but she didn’t press send.”After posting the video, Hooson, whoshareshis passion for home design and cycling to his 224,000 Instagram followers, says he lost a “good 50 to 100” followers. He called the term “pervert glasses” a “defence mechanism” to dissuade people from using them. “If everybody gets round that they are pervert glasses, which evidently they have, then it’s a really easy way of limiting sales and the usage of them,” he says. “People do not need any more of their privacy stripped away. I’m fully in support of that.”Could Meta’s ‘pervert glasses’ be banned across the UK? – The LatestRead moreHis interest in the glasses, which he received at a PR event, was far more innocent. “I saw [chefs at] high-end restaurants filming themselves with the glasses on, showing off their process. It was stupid, poetic and beautiful to watch. I wanted to have a play about and show people the things that I enjoy doing,” he says, adding that it is very hard to capture a point of view (POV) angle otherwise. “It was intended as a simple way of capturing a human POV of my morning coffee routine or my fast cycling descents. I think that’s vastly different from somebody going into the centre of Soho and asking somebody a divisive question and clipping them up for views without their knowledge,” he says.But, for now, it’s not worth using the glasses. “Would I rather just not have that little fun point-of-view shot for the greater good? Yes, I would definitely get rid of them,” he says.While the glasses have proved unpopular with some online, they sold 7m pairs in 2025 alone. Meta says the tiny, flashing LED light that activates on the glasses will let people know when they are being filmed, but there have beenmultiple instancesof people complaining they have been videoed without prior knowledge.In one instance, a woman told the BBC a man had recorded her, and thendemanded moneyto remove the videos from social media. Another womandescribed being recordedduring sexual encounters without her consent. Last month, police in Scotland said they wereinvestigating a far-right TikTokerwho allegedly filmed himself making sexualised comments to young women and telling a Sikh shopkeeper about a plan to “breed out the white race” without their knowledge.Restaurants, theatres and pubs in the UK, including Wetherspoons, have even joined in on the backlash,banning the Meta glassesover privacy fears.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFirst EditionOur morning email breaks down the key stories of the day, telling you what’s happening and why it mattersPreview latestEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionTell us: do you believe you have been filmed by Meta’s smartglasses without your consent?Read moreDeena Lang, a parenting influencer, first got her hands on a pair of the glasses from Meta. “I didn’t really know what they were capable of,” she says, but she thought they could be a cool gadget for her son. This was especially true as the family were heading to Europe for a trip and the glasses could, very usefully, translate foreign text live.But things took a turn when Lang wore them to a cooking class. After looking at the footage she had captured, she says she was “horrified because I just kept catching people giving me dirty looks or side-eye. For me, that was a real awakening.” Sheposted the footageto her 110,000 followers on Instagram with faces blurred out to act as a “cautionary tale”. She was soon flooded with comments criticising the glasses.She says she felt “a lot of embarrassment” for using them in a public place in the first instance but understood where the criticism had come from, especially after looking at how they are used in nefarious ways. “I still think they can be used for good. People who are blind said the glasses had helped them navigate life better but the negatives just far outweigh the positives,” she says. “I heard from some people who were dancers that men were invading their privacy and wearing them into the clubs. Others said they caught their waxers wearing them during appointments.“I don’t believe that we are in an age where technology like this can exist without people with bad intentions making use of it.”As for now, the glasses remain out of sight. “They’re in a drawer,” she says.A Meta spokesperson said: “We designed our AI glasses with privacy and safety features built in from the start – informed by engagement with safety experts, including women’s safety organisations. Our glasses have always had an LED light that activates whenever someone captures a photo or video for their gallery.“They also feature tamper detection technology, and we are updating the glasses to disable the camera if they detect the LED was physically tampered with or destroyed. No other kind of camera has done this and we’re proud to lead the industry forward.”Explore more on these topicsMetaPrivacySurveillanceSocial mediaDigital mediafeaturesShareReuse this content

title: The Democratic party needs to do more than represent wealthy progressives | Dustin Guastella | The Guardian
description: New research shows that a class gap on the left threatens any winning coalition – but there are ways to address it
Author: Dustin Guastella
Headline: New research shows that a class gap on the left threatens any winning coalition – but there are ways to address it
Content: ‘Maybe professional-class progressives could learn a thing or two from their working-class counterparts.’Photograph: Justin Lane/EPAView image in fullscreen‘Maybe professional-class progressives could learn a thing or two from their working-class counterparts.’Photograph: Justin Lane/EPAOpinionDemocratsThe Democratic party needs to do more than represent wealthy progressivesDustin GuastellaNew research shows that a class gap on the left threatens any winning coalition – but there are ways to address itSun 9 Aug 2026 06.00 EDTLast modified on Sun 9 Aug 2026 14.59 EDTShareDebates on the left are typically framed as a division between moderates and progressives, with the two sides wrestling over how best to form a governing coalition. Yet, in many ways, this divide obscures a much bigger fault line: the class divide. The fact is, many of the Democratic party’s ideological factions consist almost exclusively of college-educated professionals. As a result, the priorities of this class tend to dominate the party’s appeals.
